items.description: An accepted POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments writes exactly one stock_adjustments row carrying the submitted actor, quantity_before equal to the prior stored quantity and quantity_after equal to the new stored quantity (seeded with a per-run-unique sku, delta-scoped to that record)
The created_at of an adjustment written by an accepted POST is assigned by the database server clock, within the test's own before/after now() window, not by the client

An accepted adjustment updates the stock_records quantity and inserts its stock_adjustments entry in one transaction, so the stored quantity never changes without a matching audit row, verified directly against the branch database
POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments responds with Content-Type application/json for an accepted, a 422 and a 404 outcome, never text/html

In a real browser against the live DB (Playwright e2e), submitting a new quantity in the inline adjust row shows it in stock-cell-quantity before the response arrives, and page.url() is unchanged with no navigation/reload (unique crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed sku)
The inline adjust row, once the real API responds, shows the server-returned record.quantity in stock-cell-quantity

Through the real <App> at route `/` in a browser against the live DB, submitting a new quantity and actor in the row's adjust-row-<sku>-<location> form shows the new value in stock-cell-quantity before the response, with no page reload and no navigation (sku is a crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed key used in the create fill and the locators)

Through the real <App> at route `/` in a browser against the live DB, after an adjustment the row's stock-cell-quantity settles on the server-returned quantity, which matches the stored value on re-reading the stock list (unique crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed sku)

An accepted POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments returns 200 JSON whose record.quantity equals the newly stored quantity (the server-returned value the row's stock-cell-quantity settles on after the optimistic update)
POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments with a negative quantity on a uniquely-keyed seeded record returns 422 whose errors[] names the 'quantity' field
After a rejected negative-quantity adjustment, re-reading the record via the API shows the stored quantity is still the original Q
After a rejected negative-quantity adjustment, GET /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments returns an empty list (no audit entry written)
POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments with the quantity field omitted returns 422 whose errors[] names the 'quantity' field
POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments with quantity exactly 0 (boundary) returns 200 with record.quantity 0 and the stored quantity is 0

The adjustment service, called with its required injected session and a negative new quantity, rejects the write naming 'quantity' while the repository write functions (quantity update, adjustment insert) are patched and asserted never called
POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments with quantity < 0 returns 422 whose errors[] names 'quantity' and the stored quantity stays Q on the branch database
A direct INSERT into stock_adjustments with a negative quantity_before is rejected by the CHECK ck_stock_adjustments_quantities_non_negative

POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments with quantity < 0 returns 422 with errors[] naming 'quantity', and re-reading the record via the API returns the stored quantity Q (the server state the UI reverts stock-cell-quantity to and shows field-error-quantity from)
The inline adjust row, given a real-API 422 for a below-zero quantity, shows field-error-quantity naming quantity and reverts stock-cell-quantity to the stored Q
A rejected adjustment (negative quantity) leaves stock_records quantity and the stock_adjustments row count for that record unchanged on the branch database (delta-scoped to a per-run-unique sku)

The adjustment service, called with its required injected session and a blank or whitespace-only actor, rejects the write naming 'actor' while the repository write functions are patched and asserted never called
POST /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments with a blank actor returns 422 whose errors[] names 'actor'
A direct INSERT into stock_adjustments with an empty-string actor is rejected by the CHECK ck_stock_adjustments_actor_not_blank
A direct INSERT into stock_adjustments with a NULL actor is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint
The inline adjust row submitted with a blank actor shows field-error-actor naming actor, with stock-cell-quantity unchanged
A rejected adjustment (blank actor) leaves stock_records quantity and the stock_adjustments row count for that record unchanged on the branch database (delta-scoped to a per-run-unique sku)

Through the real <App> at route `/` in a browser against the live DB, submitting an adjustment with the actor left blank shows field-error-actor naming the actor field and leaves stock-cell-quantity at the stored value (unique crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed sku)
GET /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments returns every seeded adjustment with created_at, actor, quantity_before and quantity_after, ordered by created_at ascending then id
GET /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments responds with Content-Type application/json for a 200 and a 404 outcome, never text/html

With seeded stock_records rows (per-run-unique skus), downgrading to the stock_adjustments migration's own down_revision then upgrade head leaves every seeded stock_records row unchanged and recreates stock_adjustments with its columns, FK, checks and history index (explicit revision id, marked @pytest.mark.migration)
The S4 alembic upgrade() functions contain only additive operations (create_table, create_index, trigger/function creation), no drop_column, drop_table or alter type
A direct INSERT into stock_adjustments referencing a nonexistent stock_record_id is rejected by the foreign key
A direct INSERT into stock_adjustments omitting created_at stores a non-null DB-assigned timestamp from the server DEFAULT now()
A direct INSERT into stock_adjustments with a NULL quantity_before is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint

The adjustment-history panel for a record with seeded adjustments renders one history-entry-<n> per adjustment in time order, each with history-timestamp, history-actor, history-qty-before, history-qty-after
The adjustment-history panel for a record with no adjustments renders the history-empty empty-state instead of a blank table

Through the real <App> at route `/` in a browser against the live DB, opening history-toggle-<sku>-<location> after accepted adjustments shows the adjustment-history panel with one history-entry-<n> per adjustment (unique crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed sku)

Through the real <App> at route `/` in a browser against the live DB, each history-entry-<n> shows history-timestamp, history-actor, history-qty-before and history-qty-after in time order matching the adjustments entered (unique crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed sku)
After a refused DELETE of an adjustment, GET /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments still lists the entry with its original timestamp, actor and quantity_before/after
DELETE /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments/{adjustment_id} returns 405 with a JSON detail, the entry's timestamp, actor and quantities unchanged afterwards
PUT /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments/{adjustment_id} returns 405 with a JSON detail, the entry unchanged afterwards
PATCH /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments/{adjustment_id} returns 405 with a JSON detail, the entry unchanged afterwards
The 405 response of the adjustment-mutation path has Content-Type application/json, never text/html
A direct UPDATE of an existing stock_adjustments entry's created_at is refused by trigger trg_stock_adjustments_no_update, the row unchanged on re-read
The adjustment entry path advertises no mutation: an OPTIONS/Allow check on /api/stock-records/{id}/adjustments/{adjustment_id} lists none of PUT, PATCH, DELETE
